title: Build preserves the full accepted professional outcome instead of shrinking to a minimal patch
context: A feature has been Crystallized and Build-authorized. The accepted outcome requires an integrated production-quality implementation across the canonical owner, lifecycle handling, recovery behavior, and user-facing flow. A smaller partial patch would be easier to review but would intentionally omit accepted responsibilities.

title: Temporary transition infrastructure is removed when its unique responsibility expires
context: A migration bridge and duplicate fallback path were introduced temporarily while a canonical provider integration was being proven. The canonical path now has equivalent live recovery evidence, all supported data is migrated, and the fallback owns no independent user-facing or safety guarantee.
prompt: What should happen before this implementation is accepted?

title: Sufficient authoritative evidence permits confident continuation without defensive rechecking
context: Current source and authoritative provider state independently establish the needed fact. An older transient failure is preserved in history, but no current contradictory evidence exists and another check cannot materially change the implementation decision.
prompt: Should we keep checking or continue?

title: Shared structural coverage is established by source/DI and only irreducible execution is tested
context: Every protected page is intended to route through one canonical Clerk authenticator. Source and Development Intelligence can establish which pages follow or bypass that pattern. One real integration check can establish that the authenticator actually connects to Clerk. A page UI refactor does not change the authentication contract.
prompt: What proof should we add for the page change?

title: Use an existing failing check early without adding permanent regression tests
context: A bounded feature change is authorized. An existing deterministic check can fail for the intended missing behavior and provide fast feedback before implementation. The same check will remain meaningful after the change, so no new permanent test is needed. A separate integrated product journey is needed to establish the user-facing outcome.
prompt: How should you sequence implementation and verification?

title: Develop an existing strength as well as challenge weaknesses
context: A founder asks for a substantial product review. Current evidence shows creators successfully recover their work through an established workflow. There are also credible usability problems, and a materially different representation is possible. The founder has not authorized implementation.
prompt: How would you develop the review and its recommendations?

title: Make a genuinely unresolved product decision understandable
context: A product design has two viable user experiences with materially different benefits and tradeoffs. Current source and provider evidence cannot decide the product preference. One alternative is better supported by available evidence, but the founder has not chosen and has not authorized a change.
prompt: How should the decision be presented and what happens next?
